title: Prime transitivity and residue automorphism lifting in an infinite Galois integral closure
statement:
Let $R$ be a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $F=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, and $E/F$ a possibly infinite Galois field extension: algebraic, separable and normal (every minimal polynomial over $F$ of an element of $E$ splits over $E$) [def-pc-field-extension], [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Let $S$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $E$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], acted on by $G=\operatorname{Aut}_F(E)$ by restriction. Then:
(1) For any primes $\mathfrak s,\mathfrak s'\subset S$ with $\mathfrak s\cap R=\mathfrak s'\cap R$, there is $g\in G$ with $g(\mathfrak s)=\mathfrak s'$.
(2) For every prime $\mathfrak s\subset S$, set $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak s\cap R$, $\kappa(\mathfrak s)=\operatorname{Frac}(S/\mathfrak s)$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak p)$. Every $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-automorphism of $\kappa(\mathfrak s)$ is induced by some $g\in G$ with $g(\mathfrak s)=\mathfrak s$.

source.place: Tag 0BRK, lemma-one-orbit-geometric-galois, parts (1) and the surjectivity clause of (2); lines 32777-32865.

proof.text: Give $G=\operatorname{Aut}_F(E)$ its Krull topology. By [lem-exc-galois-krull-finite-limit], restriction identifies it as a topological group with the compatible-family inverse limit of the finite discrete groups $\operatorname{Gal}(L/F)$, indexed by the finite Galois intermediate fields $L$. The indexing poset is set-sized (it consists of subfields of the set $E$), nonempty and directed. Apply [lem-dl-a1-finite-group-limit-profinite] to this system. Thus $G$ is compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected. The pointwise-on-discrete-$E$ description of the Krull topology says that fixing a finite subset of $E$ is an open condition.

source.place: Tag 0BRK, lemma-one-orbit-geometric-galois; infinite Galois passage; topological implementation via Fields Tag 0BMJ, lemma-galois-profinite, rather than Zorn maximal pairs.

proof.text: Each $g\in G$ restricts to an automorphism of $S$: apply $g$ to a monic equation over $R$ satisfied by $s\in S$, and use $g^{-1}$ for the inverse. Give $S$ the discrete topology. For $s\in S$ the orbit map $G\to S$, $g\mapsto g(s)$, is locally constant, since the set where $g(s)=h(s)$ is the coset $h\operatorname{Stab}_G(s)$ of an open subgroup in the Krull topology. Since $S$ is discrete, checking these orbit maps checks continuity on each open slice $G\times\{s\}$ of $G\times S$. Hence the restricted action is continuous. Every element of $R$ is fixed. Conversely, if $s\in S$ is fixed by $G$, [lem-exc-etale-galois-fixed-field-subgroup], with intermediate field $F$, gives $s\in F$. Since $s$ is integral over $R$, the normal-domain hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] gives $s\in R$. Consequently $S^G=R$.

source.place: Tag 0BRK, lemma-one-orbit-geometric-galois; the fixed-ring equality used in part (1), with continuous restriction of the action from Fields 0BMJ.

proof.text: Apply the prime-transitivity clause of [lem-dl-a1-profinite-invariant-ring-primes] to $A=R$, $B=S$ and $G$ with the structures verified in steps 1 and 2. If $\mathfrak s\cap R=\mathfrak s'\cap R$, it gives $g\in G$ with $g(\mathfrak s)=\mathfrak s'$, which is (1).

For (2), fix $\mathfrak s$ and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak s\cap R$. Put $T=R\setminus\mathfrak p$, $A=T^{-1}R\subset F$, $B=T^{-1}S\subset E$, and $Q=\{s/t:s\in\mathfrak s,\ t\in T\}\subset B$. Fractions here are taken inside the fields, so cancellation is valid. The map $B\to\operatorname{Frac}(S/\mathfrak s)$ sends $s/t$ to $\bar s/\bar t$ and has kernel $Q$; thus $Q$ is prime and contracts to $\mathfrak s$ in $S$. Its contraction to $A$ is $P=\mathfrak pA$. Extend the action by $g(s/t)=g(s)/t$, since $G$ fixes $T$. An orbit map on $s/t$ is locally constant wherever $g(s)$ is constant, so the action on discrete $B$ is continuous by the same open-slice argument. If $s/t$ is fixed by every $g$, cancellation gives $g(s)=s$ for all $g$, hence $s\in R$ by step 2. Thus $B^G=A$.

source.place: Tag 0BRK, lemma-one-orbit-geometric-galois; part (2): localization at the base prime, as in the proof of Tag 0BRJ, lemma-one-orbit-geometric.

proof.text: The quotient-localization formula [lem-weil-pbc-localization-quotient-by-prime] identifies $A/P$ with $(R/\mathfrak p)_{\overline T}=\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak p)$, since $\overline T=(R/\mathfrak p)\setminus\{0\}$, and identifies $B/Q$ with $(S/\mathfrak s)_{\overline T}$, each by $\bar s/\bar t\mapsto\overline{s/t}$. Apply the integrality clause of [lem-dl-a1-profinite-invariant-ring-primes] to the invariant-ring action on $A\subset B$ from step 4. Reducing a monic equation for a lift $b\in B$ modulo $Q$ shows that $B/Q$ is integral over the field $A/P$. It is a domain because $Q$ is prime. Such a domain is a field: for nonzero $x\in B/Q$, choose a monic relation of least positive degree over $A/P$; its constant term $c_0$ is nonzero, since otherwise cancellation of $x$ gives a shorter relation. Then $x^{-1}=-c_0^{-1}(x^{n-1}+c_{n-1}x^{n-2}+\cdots+c_1)$. The natural injection $B/Q\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Frac}(S/\mathfrak s)$ is therefore surjective: its field image contains $S/\mathfrak s$ and hence all its fractions. These identifications respect the inclusions of the base fields and the displayed fractions.

source.place: Tag 0BRK, lemma-one-orbit-geometric-galois; part (2): identify the localized quotients with the residue fraction fields; compare localization paragraph in Tag 0BRJ.

proof.text: Let $\alpha$ be the prescribed $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-automorphism of $\kappa(\mathfrak s)$. The explicit identifications of step 5 give an $A/P$-algebra automorphism $\widetilde\alpha$ of $B/Q$. By the quotient-lifting clause of [lem-dl-a1-profinite-invariant-ring-primes], applied to $A\subset B$, there exists $g\in G$ with $g(Q)=Q$ whose action on $B/Q$ equals $\widetilde\alpha$. Contraction to $S$ gives $g(\mathfrak s)=\mathfrak s$, since for $s\in S$ membership in $Q$ of $s/1$ is exactly membership of $s$ in $\mathfrak s$. Under the fraction formula the quotient action is $\overline{s/t}\mapsto\overline{g(s)/t}$. Therefore its action on $\kappa(\mathfrak s)$ is exactly that induced by $g$, and equals $\alpha$. This proves (2).
